Name: Neutralization
Description: Strong acid + strong base gives salt + water. Exothermic.

Name: Precipitation (AgCl)
Description: White curdy AgCl precipitate settles at bottom.

Name: HCl Gas Evolution
Description: HCl gas released. Pungent, white fumes in moist air.

Name: No Reaction
Description: Both stay dissolved. Blue color persists.

Name: Indicator - Pink
Description: Phenolphthalein turns deep pink in basic solution.

Name: Indicator - Colorless
Description: Phenolphthalein remains colorless in acidic solution.

Name: No Reaction
Description: Both ions remain in solution. Blue color stays.

Name: No Reaction
Description: Both are strong electrolytes. No reaction.

Name: No Reaction
Description: Ethanol is a very weak acid. No reaction at room temp.

Name: Brown Precipitate (Ag2O)
Description: Violent reaction! Brown Ag2O precipitates with intense heat.

Name: VIOLENT: Sodium + Water
Description: Sodium dances on water surface, H2 ignites with bright yellow flame (Na+), NaOH forms. Extremely exothermic.

Name: Magnesium + Water
Description: Mg reacts very slowly with cold water. Fast with hot water/steam.

Name: VIOLENT: Sodium + HCl
Description: Sodium in HCl causes explosive H2 release with orange-yellow flame. More vigorous than water.

Name: Magnesium + HCl
Description: Magnesium burns with a brilliant white flame in acid!

Name: VIOLENT: Sodium + H2SO4
Description: Extremely violent! Sodium in sulfuric acid detonates with intense yellow flame and dense smoke.

Name: Magnesium + H2SO4
Description: Bright white flame with intense heat and smoke.

Name: Golden Rain (Lead Iodide)
Description: Brilliant yellow PbI2 precipitate forms instantly, settling as golden rain.

Name: Copper + Silver Nitrate
Description: Silver crystals form on copper. Solution turns blue.

Name: Zinc Displacement
Description: Blue color fades as zinc displaces copper.

Name: Iron Displacement
Description: Blue solution turns green as iron displaces copper.

Name: Purple Fades (KMnO4 + H2O2)
Description: Purple permanganate reduced to colorless Mn2+. Oxygen gas released. Classic redox demo.

Name: Elephant Toothpaste (with soap)
Description: Rapid foam eruption! Potassium iodide catalyzes peroxide breakdown.

Name: Zinc + Hydrochloric Acid
Description: Vigorous hydrogen bubbles. Classic lab reaction.

Name: Iron + Hydrochloric Acid
Description: Steady hydrogen bubbles. Solution turns pale green.

Name: Marble + HCl (Volcano)
Description: Vigorous bubbling like a volcano! CO2 released.

Name: Barium Sulfate Precipitate
Description: Dense white precipitate of barium sulfate.

Name: Ammonium Chloride (Neutralization)
Description: White smoke of ammonium chloride forms.

Name: Two-Stage: Blue ppt â†’ Deep Blue Complex
Description: Light blue Cu(OH)2 ppt forms, then dissolves in excess NH3 to deep navy [Cu(NH3)4]2+ complex.

Name: Orange to Green (Breathalyzer)
Description: Orange dichromate reduced to green Cr3+. Breathalyzer!

Name: Amphoteric Reaction
Description: Aluminum dissolves in base. H2 released.

Name: Ammonia Gas Released
Description: Pungent ammonia gas. Test for NH4+.

Name: VIOLENT: Potassium + Water
Description: More violent than sodium! Lilac flame (K+), H2 ignites instantly, KOH forms.

Name: Calcium + Water
Description: Slower than sodium. Bubbles + milky solution.

Name: Slow Bubbles (Pb)
Description: Initial bubbles, then PbCl2 coating slows reaction.

Name: White Precipitate (AgCl)
Description: White curdy AgCl precipitate. Test for chloride.

Name: Lime Burning (CaO)
Description: Limestone decomposes at 825C (industrial calcination). Requires strong heat.

Name: Baking Soda Decomposition
Description: Baking soda decomposes on heating. Requires heat.

Name: Silver Nitrate Decomposition
Description: AgNO3 decomposes at 440C to silver + brown NO2 gas.

Name: White Precipitate (BaSO4)
Description: White BaSO4 precipitate. Test for sulfate.

Name: Iodoform Test (Yellow)
Description: Yellow CHI3 precipitate. Test for methyl ketone.

Name: Black Charring
Description: Black carbon column. Sulfuric acid dehydrates sugar.

Name: Benzoate Neutralization
Description: Benzoic acid dissolves. Sodium benzoate forms.

Name: PURPLE FIRE BLAST
Description: White smoke first, then crackling sparks ignite into a bright purple flame. Strongly exothermic.

Name: Titration Endpoint
Description: Indicator turns pink at endpoint. NaOH in excess.

Name: Competitive Precipitation
Description: AgCl precipitates first (Ksp lower). Cu stays in solution.

Name: Sequential Neutralization
Description: Base neutralizes acid first, then precipitates Cu(OH)2.

Name: Neutralization with spectator
Description: NaCl is spectator ion. Reaction proceeds normally.
